title: 1950 AHSME Problem 33

concepts.label: Power scaling of length, area, and volume

statement: The number of circular pipes with an inside diameter of \(1\) inch which will carry the same amount of water as a pipe with an inside diameter of \(6\) inches is:

solutions.text:
The ratio of the diameters is \(6:1,\) so the ratio of cross-sectional areas is \[ 6^2:1^2=36:1. \] Thus \(36\) of the smaller pipes have the same total cross-sectional area as the larger pipe.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Water-carrying capacity is proportional to cross-sectional area
Circular area scales as the square of the diameter
